properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. flo2's proposal, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-21, in flo2's words: "Accept a caller identity at the handshake and remember it for the session. flo2 passes the signed-in person; reflow2 takes it on trust."

THE NEED IS REAL AND THIS DESIGN HAS ALREADY MEASURED IT. reflow2 has no notion of a CURRENT contributor, so every authorship write is an explicit argument somebody has to remember, and the consequence was counted on 2026-08-10: 0 of 360 ChangeEvents carried an author at all. flo2 is offering the fact reflow2 is missing.

⚠️ FIRST, TWO DIFFERENT THINGS ARE BEING FUSED, and keeping them apart is most of the answer.
· A SEAT is which session is talking — machine:pid:mint. It exists for CONCURRENCY: who holds which claim, which writes are whose on a shared server. It is deliberately advisory and released at checkout.
· A CONTRIBUTOR is whose WORD a node is. It exists for AUTHORITY: an approver edge is the signature the intent-authority gate checks.
flo2 says "the signed-in person", which is a Contributor, and "remember it for the session", which is seat machinery. Wiring the second to the first is the actual proposal, and it is the part with consequences.

🛑 IT CONTRADICTS A SETTLED CHOICE, AND THE CONTRADICTION IS NARROW BUT REAL. Anthony chose mint-and-carry on 2026-07-30: a seat is minted on request and carried as a tool argument, and a claim-family call arriving without one is REFUSED BY NAME rather than served from remembered state. The backstop was called the load-bearing half, because every quiet alternative lets the call SUCCEED with a wrong identity. "Remember it for the session" is remembered state. Note it is NOT the same as rejected option (b) — that derived a seat from transport headers, and flo2's identity is explicitly ASSERTED by the client, which is a genuinely different and better-founded thing. But the sessionless MCP transport the 2026-07-28 revision introduces has no session to remember anything on, which is exactly what `req:seat-identity-survives-stateless-mcp` was written to guard.

🛑 AND "ON TRUST" HAS A PRICE THAT DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON THE USE. This design has one ENFORCED rule — design intent moves only on the owner's word — and a CI gate that fails the build on a settled node with no approver. If a caller-asserted identity can become an approver, that gate's guarantee is only as strong as the honesty of whatever client connected, and reflow2 has no authentication at all today (the hosted surface ships read-only precisely because of that). Trust is cheap for "who wrote this" and expensive for "who approved this".

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) ACCEPT IT FOR ATTRIBUTION ONLY — a handshake-supplied identity may become the `author` on writes it makes, and may NEVER become an `approver`. A settling status still needs the approver named explicitly in that call, as it does today. This gets flo2 the thing they actually asked for and costs the authority rule nothing.
(b) ACCEPT IT FOR BOTH, and say plainly on the record that approver authority is now delegated to the client's own sign-in. Defensible when the client genuinely authenticates its person; indefensible as a silent default.
(c) MINT-AND-CARRY, EXTENDED — keep the settled shape and add a contributor to what the seat carries, so identity travels as an argument rather than as remembered state. Consistent with the 2026-07-28 direction, and it costs flo2 an argument on calls that care.
(d) DECLINE, and keep explicit authorship arguments.

AN HONEST NOTE ON WHERE IT IS REMEMBERED: reflow2 already keeps per-session state — a seat is minted per client and survives the transport — so "remember it" is not new machinery. The objection is not feasibility; it is what the remembered value is then allowed to authorise.

═══ ADDENDUM 2026-09-21, AFTER READING FLO2's OWN WRITE-UP (F31) RATHER THAN THE TWO-LINE RELAY ═══

⭐ TWO CORRECTIONS TO WHAT IS WRITTEN ABOVE, both in flo2's favour.

**1. THE ATTRIBUTION / AUTHENTICATION SPLIT IS THEIRS, MADE EXPLICITLY, AND THIS NODE IMPLIED THEY HAD MISSED IT.** F31 states it as the heading of its own section: "What flo2 needs is ATTRIBUTION, not AUTHENTICATION — and conflating them is what made this look expensive." Authentication is proving identity, belongs at flo2's gateway, and they name `dec:connector-is-a-product-surface-over-the-engine` themselves to say reflow2 should never grow it — "that decision is not being reopened". Attribution is being TOLD a name by something already trusted: no verification, no keys, no OAuth. The worry recorded above about reflow2 having no authentication is therefore answering a question flo2 did not ask.

**2. THE TRUST IS BOUNDED BY A CONSTRAINT THIS DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS.** Their argument: `con:nothing-public-proxies-to-reflow2-until-a-gateway-authenticates` means nothing but flo2 can reach reflow2 at all, so believing what flo2 says costs nothing that was not already the case. The expensive half is solved on their side and reflow2 gets the answer free.

🛑 AND THE BIGGER FINDING: THIS QUESTION WAS ALREADY OPEN HERE, A MONTH EARLIER, WITH MORE IN IT. `dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id` (Anthony, 2026-08-26) already draws exactly F31's split — *"Middleware removes the authentication problem and leaves the ATTRIBUTION problem exactly where it was. They look like one problem and they are two"* — and already records that a caller-supplied contributor_id is sound on a loopback surface precisely because anyone who can call that server can already edit the graph file directly. It carries four options this node re-derived three of. Its option **(d) — the remote surface may PROPOSE, never SETTLE** is a better answer to the attribution-versus-authority question than option (a) above, and it needs no new vocabulary: `proposed` versus `accepted` already exists and the intent-authority gate already enforces it.

⇒ The duplicate guard did not surface that node when this one was written, and nothing about the wording would have led a reader from one to the other. They are now linked rather than merged, because they were written for different reasons and both reasons matter: that one holds Anthony's reasoning about where authentication lives, this one holds flo2's field case and its cost.

⚠️ WHAT STILL STANDS FROM ABOVE, UNCHANGED: the seat-versus-contributor distinction, and the observation that the settled mint-and-carry shape refuses rather than remembers. F31 asks for "a `contributor_id` (or a seat bound to one) supplied at `initialize`, or settable once per session" — the parenthesis is the reconciliation, and it is close to option (c).

properties.rationale: Recorded open, and recorded as a question about USE rather than about acceptance, because the proposal's cost is entirely in what the identity is permitted to sign. Option (a) appears to cost nothing and deliver the reported need, which is a strong hint — but it is a hint about Anthony's own enforced rule, so it is his to rule on and not mine to assume.
